title: Strangler-fig decomposition: facade, branch by abstraction, parallel run, cut-over
description: Move the monolith's fine rule into its own service behind a strangler facade, compare both in a parallel run, and cut over only when a measured mismatch rate allows it.
outcome: You can design an incremental extraction (seam, facade, shadow, canary, service), turn cut-over criteria into code, measure a mismatch rate and keep new code from calling the legacy module with a ratchet fitness function.
environment: Python 3.12 standard library only (validated on 3.12.15 / Linux, SQLite 3.44.0); unittest. Targets: Apple-silicon Mac mini (zsh) and Windows 11 PC (PowerShell); no new packages beyond L100.
overview: strangler.py routes fine calls legacy -> shadow -> canary -> service; the parallel run returns the legacy answer and logs differences.
The extracted service rounds half-cents to even, the monolith rounds them up: 108 of 2,000 seeded requests differ.
prerequisites: Lesson 3 (module boundaries and their fitness function)

designBrief.context: The fines rule lives in the Library Loans monolith with two direct callers. A team wants to own and deploy it as a service; nobody documented all its rules.
constraints: 0 members charged a different fine because of the migration
cut over only with >= 1,000 compared requests, mismatch rate <= 0.1 %, 0 candidate errors
no new code may import legacy_monolith (callers may only decrease)
trunk stays releasable during the change
designBrief.question: How do we move fine traffic from the monolith to the extracted service, and when is it safe to switch?

options.name: Big-bang switch
options.description: Deploy the service and point all callers at it at once.
options.evidence: failure_lab.py: 108 of 2,000 seeded requests (5.4 %) would get a different fine; found only after members are charged.
options.verdict: Rejected: the rounding difference reaches members.

options.name: Facade + parallel run (shadow) + canary
options.description: Branch by abstraction (FinesPort), facade routes legacy/shadow/canary/service; shadow returns legacy and logs differences.
options.evidence: app.py: shadow found the same 108 mismatches, members saw 0; after the fix 0 mismatches over 2,000 -> cutover ready; canary 10 % = 34 of 500 requests (sticky per member). Over HTTP 3.0-26.6 s per 2,000 shadow calls on this shared host.

options.name: Branch by abstraction only, in-process
options.description: Keep the new implementation inside the monolith behind the port and flip a flag.
options.evidence: Same comparison results in-process (failure_lab.py, no network); but no independent deploy, which was the goal.
options.verdict: Kept as the first step (the seam); not the end state.

fitnessFunction.what: No new code imports legacy_monolith; the known callers in legacy_callers.json may only shrink (ratchet).

scalingLimits: Shadow mode doubles work; at high traffic sample the shadow calls or run them asynchronously - signal: p99 of the facade rises while shadowing.
Only side-effect-free operations can be shadowed; writes need idempotent dual writes and reconciliation - signal: duplicate emails or charges.
Non-deterministic outputs (timestamps, ordering) inflate the mismatch rate - signal: mismatches without a business pattern in mismatches.jsonl.

glossary.meaning: Replace a system gradually by growing new code around it and moving traffic slice by slice.
Put an interface between callers and a supplier so two implementations coexist on trunk.
Run old and new, return the old answer, compare and record differences.
A fitness baseline that may only improve, e.g. a list of legacy callers that can only shrink.

concepts: Move traffic, not code: a facade decides per request who answers.
Cut-over criteria are code: evidence count, mismatch rate, errors.
Transitional architecture must be removed; a ratchet keeps it shrinking.

title: Multi-tenancy: shared schema vs schema per tenant vs database per tenant
description: Store 50 libraries in three tenancy layouts on SQLite files, measure isolation, noisy neighbour and migration effort, and enforce tenant-scoped queries with a static fitness test and a runtime guard.
outcome: You can compare tenancy layouts with measured evidence, choose one with an ADR, and make 'no query without a tenant id' a fitness function that fails the build.
environment: Python 3.12 standard library only (validated on 3.12.15 / Linux, SQLite 3.44.0); unittest. Targets: Apple-silicon Mac mini (zsh) and Windows 11 PC (PowerShell); no new packages beyond L100.
overview: tenancy.py builds the same loans data as shared schema, schema per tenant and database per tenant and measures each.
A new overdue report forgot `WHERE tenant_id`: 686 of 700 rows it returns belong to other libraries.
prerequisites: Lesson 10 (identity: where the tenant id comes from)

designBrief.context: Library Loans becomes a hosted service: 50 small libraries now, a few large ones later, one codebase.
constraints: 0 rows of another library visible to any query
one schema change must not need 50 migrations for small libraries
a bulk import of one library must not block other libraries that need write isolation
every query provably tenant-scoped (CI gate)
designBrief.question: Which data layout per tenant, and how do we guarantee that no query crosses tenants?

options.name: Shared schema (tenant_id column)
options.description: One table; every query filters by tenant_id; tenant first in every index.
options.evidence: app.py, 50 libraries: one missing filter leaked 686 of 700 rows; 20 of 20 neighbour writes blocked during a bulk import; 1 DDL statement / 1 file per schema change.
options.verdict: Chosen as the default tier, with both guards (ADR 0002).

options.name: Schema per tenant (table per tenant in one file)
options.description: Names separate tenants; SQLite has no CREATE SCHEMA, ATTACH allows 10 databases by default.
options.evidence: 0 leaked rows (guard still flags the query); 20 of 20 writes blocked (same file); 50 DDL statements; try-it: the 11th ATTACH fails 'too many attached databases - max 10'.
options.verdict: Rejected: migration fan-out without write isolation.

options.name: Database per tenant (one SQLite file each)
options.evidence: 0 leaked rows; 0 of 20 writes blocked; 50 DDL statements / 50 files (0.45-4.5 s here vs 9-54 ms shared).
options.verdict: Premium tier for libraries that need write isolation or their own restore.

fitnessFunction.what: No SQL on a tenant table without `WHERE tenant_id = ?` (static, AST over string constants) and no executed statement without the current tenant's id (TenantGuard, runtime).

scalingLimits: Shared SQLite file: one writer at a time for all tenants - signal: 'database is locked' and rising write latency during imports.
Database per tenant: migrations and connections fan out (5,000 tenants = 5,000 migrations) - signal: tenants on different schema versions.
Hot tenant in the shared schema - signal: one tenant_id dominates rows, writes or p99.

concepts: The tenancy boundary is a WHERE clause, a name, or a connection.

title: Policy as code: RBAC vs ABAC, policy tests and decision logs
description: Move Library Loans' authorization rules into a Rego policy file evaluated by a decision point, test it with requirement cases, log every decision, and compare RBAC with ABAC.
outcome: You can separate enforcement (PEP) from decisions (PDP), express attribute rules as policy, prove them with policy tests and coverage, write privacy-safe decision logs, and know when RBAC is enough.
environment: Python 3.12 standard library only (validated on 3.12.15 / Linux, SQLite 3.44.0); unittest. Targets: Apple-silicon Mac mini (zsh) and Windows 11 PC (PowerShell); no new packages beyond L100. Optional: OPA 1.21.4 (Apache-2.0; brew install opa, or opa_windows_amd64.exe from the GitHub releases) for opa test / opa_parity.py.
overview: rego_lite.py evaluates policy/loans.rego (a Rego v1 subset) for 14 requirement cases; handlers call authorize() first.
A new librarian rule forgot the library check: a librarian of lib01 may view lib00's loans.

designBrief.context: Rules depend on attributes: own loans, same library, loan limit 5, suspended accounts, waivers above 20.00 need a manager. They are spread over handlers.
constraints: 14 of 14 requirement cases decided correctly
every public handler enforces a decision
every allow/deny rule covered by a case
no email address in decision logs
rules reviewable in one file

scalingLimits: rego_lite re-parses expressions per decision (290-1,145 us here) - signal: authorization shows up in latency profiles; compile once (OPA) or cache.
Remote PDP per request adds a hop and a dependency - signal: 403/500 spikes when the PDP is down; run it as a sidecar or library.

glossary.meaning: Policy enforcement point: the code that asks and enforces (here handlers.authorize).
Policy decision point: evaluates the policy and returns the decision.
Attribute-based access control: rules over subject, resource, action and environment attributes.
One structured record per decision: id, policy revision, masked input, result.

concepts: Ask in the handler, decide in the policy.
RBAC sees roles; ABAC sees attributes.
Policy tests, coverage and decision logs make rules provable and auditable.

title: Evolutionary architecture: expand/contract migrations, API versions, flags, fitness over time

outcome: You can plan a zero-downtime schema and API change, write the guard that makes the contract step safe, and use a fitness history to fail CI on any step that breaks a threshold.

overview: rollout.py upgrades 4 instances one by one while a migration plan runs; every phase serves 100 seeded requests.

title: Cost and capacity planning: Little's law, benchmarks, headroom, cost per request

title: Capstone: Library Loans, production-ready
description: Evolve Library Loans into a production-ready system: strangle the fines module, add tenancy, policy, events through an outbox, SLOs, contract tests and fitness functions, and let a scorecard decide the release.
outcome: You can integrate architectural decisions into one system, prove each with a measured criterion, run seeded faults to show the gates work, and keep the release decision in code while a local model only explains it.
environment: Python 3.12 standard library only (validated on 3.12.15 / Linux, SQLite 3.44.0); unittest. Targets: Apple-silicon Mac mini (zsh) and Windows 11 PC (PowerShell); no new packages beyond L100. Reuses labs L200 #9, L300 #14-15 and L400 #17-21 by path. architecture.summary: A member-portal request (contract-tested) reaches the HTTP adapter and LoansService. The service asks the policy decision point first (lesson 19 policy, decision log without email), then runs SQL bound to :tenant on the shared schema while TenantGuard watches every statement (lesson 18). Returns ask the strangler facade for the fine; it shadows the extracted fines service on 2,000 requests and switches to it only when the mismatch rate is 0 (lesson 17). Loan rows and events are written in one transaction to the outbox; a relay publishes at least once and idempotent consumers apply each event once (lesson 9). The request log feeds the lesson 15 SLIs; CI adds the contract, the capacity gate (lesson 21) and the ADR check, and run_capstone.py turns everything into GO or NO-GO.

code:
"""Capstone: Library Loans, production-ready. Runs everything end to end and prints the scorecard as JSON lines.

Run: python run_capstone.py                      all milestones, no faults (exit 0 = GO)
     python run_capstone.py --fault cross-tenant-policy   one seeded fault (exit 1 = NO-GO); see scorecard.FAULTS
Writes out/scorecard.jsonl, out/requests.jsonl, out/decisions.jsonl. The verdict comes from code, never from a model.
"""
import argparse
import functools
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import loans_service
import scorecard
from http_api import start
from reuse import capacity, contract, fitness_capacity, fitness_legacy, fitness_policy, rego_lite, slo

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ADR_FILES = sorted(HERE.parent.glob("*/adr/0*.md"))  # the topic's ADR log: lessons 17-21 + the capstone


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)  # deterministic (seeded simulation): compute once per process
def capacity_gate():
    return fitness_capacity.gate(capacity)


def row(milestone, criterion, measure, value, threshold, ok):
    return {"milestone": milestone, "criterion": criterion, "measure": measure, "value": value,
            "threshold": threshold, "pass": bool(ok)}


def criteria(e):
    s, rows = e["service"], []
    stats = e["cutover"]
    rows.append(row("M1 strangle", "fines parallel run", "mismatch rate over 2,000 shadow requests",
                    stats["mismatch_rate"], "<= 0.001", stats["ready"]))
    rows.append(row("M1 strangle", "fines cut over", "facade mode after the run", e["facade_mode"], "service",
                    e["facade_mode"] == "service"))
    callers = sorted(fitness_legacy.legacy_callers(HERE))
    rows.append(row("M1 strangle", "no new legacy callers", "capstone files importing legacy_monolith", callers, "[]",
                    not callers))
    rows.append(row("M2 tenancy", "tenant guard", "statements without the current tenant id",
                    len(s.guard_violations), 0, not s.guard_violations))
    unscoped = scorecard.unscoped_sql()
    rows.append(row("M2 tenancy", "tenant-scoped SQL", "loans queries without WHERE tenant_id", unscoped, "[]",
                    not unscoped))
    p = e["probes"]
    rows.append(row("M2 tenancy", "cross-library reads", "rows of another library returned", p["cross_rows"], 0,
                    p["cross_rows"] == 0))
    failed = fitness_policy.gate_policy_tests(s.pdp.policy)["value"]
    rows.append(row("M3 policy", "policy requirement cases", "cases decided as specified",
                    f"{len(fitness_policy.CASES) - len(failed)}/{len(fitness_policy.CASES)}", "14/14", not failed))
    rows.append(row("M3 policy", "cross-library probes denied", "probes allowed across libraries",
                    p["cross_allowed"], 0, p["cross_allowed"] == 0))
    gaps = scorecard.pep_gaps()
    rows.append(row("M3 policy", "every entry point enforces policy", "public methods without _authorize", gaps,
                    "[]", not gaps))
    leaked = sum('"email"' in line for line in e["decision_log"])
    rows.append(row("M3 policy", "decision log privacy", f"decisions logged {len(e['decision_log'])}, with email",
                    leaked, 0, leaked == 0 and e["decision_log"]))
    ev = e["events"]
    rows.append(row("M4 events", "outbox completeness", "committed changes vs outbox rows",
                    f"{ev['committed_changes']}/{ev['outbox_rows']}", "equal", ev["committed_changes"] == ev["outbox_rows"]))
    rows.append(row("M4 events", "relay published", "unpublished outbox rows", ev["unpublished"], 0,
                    ev["unpublished"] == 0))
    rows.append(row("M4 events", "idempotent consumers", "projection rows wrong after redelivering every event",
                    ev["projection_mismatches"], 0, ev["projection_mismatches"] == 0))
    records = slo.parse(s.request_log)
    now = records[-1]["t"] + 1
    for sli in ("availability", "latency"):
        good = 1 - slo.bad_ratio(records, sli)
        rows.append(row("M5 SLO + CI", f"{sli} SLI", f"good / valid over {len(records)} requests", round(good, 4),
                        f">= {slo.SLOS[sli]}", good >= slo.SLOS[sli]))
    alerts = slo.alerts(records, now)
    rows.append(row("M5 SLO + CI", "burn-rate alerts", "alerts firing at the end of the run", len(alerts), 0, not alerts))
    contract_pdp = rego_lite.DecisionPoint(s.pdp.policy)  # same policy; contract traffic is not logged
    server, url = start(lambda: loans_service.LoansService(contract_pdp, s.fines))
    try:
        problems = contract.verify_provider(HERE / "contracts" / "member-portal--loans-service.json", url)
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        server.server_close()
    rows.append(row("M5 SLO + CI", "consumer contract", "member-portal contract problems", problems, "[]", not problems))
    cap = capacity_gate()
    rows.append(row("M5 SLO + CI", "capacity N+1", "p99 ms with one instance down", cap["value"]["p99_one_down_ms"],
                    "<= 300", cap["ok"]))
    bad_adrs = [f.name for f in ADR_FILES if scorecard.adr_problems(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    rows.append(row("M5 SLO + CI", "ADR log", f"ADRs in Nygard format of {len(ADR_FILES)}", bad_adrs, "[]",
                    not bad_adrs and len(ADR_FILES) >= 4))
    return rows


def main(argv=None, out=sys.stdout):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--fault", choices=scorecard.FAULTS)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    rows = criteria(scorecard.build(args.fault))
    passed = sum(r["pass"] for r in rows)
    summary = {"summary": True, "fault": args.fault, "passed": passed, "total": len(rows),
               "failed": [r["criterion"] for r in rows if not r["pass"]],
               "verdict": "GO" if passed == len(rows) else "NO-GO"}  # deterministic: code decides the release
    lines = [json.dumps(r) for r in rows + [summary]]
    (HERE / "out" / "scorecard.jsonl").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("\n".join(lines), file=out)
    return 0 if summary["verdict"] == "GO" else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
